title: 5. Second Council of Constantinople (553)
about: Reading Chalcedon with St Cyril: the 'Three Chapters'.

items.text: A century after Chalcedon, the Emperor Justinian sought to heal the split over it. Some writings that leaned toward Nestorius (the 'Three Chapters': works of Theodore of Mopsuestia, writings of Theodoret against St Cyril, and a letter of Ibas) were still defended by some.

days.title: One of the Holy Trinity suffered in the flesh

items.text: The council confessed that 'one of the Holy Trinity was crucified in the flesh'. We sing it at every Liturgy in the hymn 'Only-begotten Son', said to be written by Justinian himself.
The council condemned the Three Chapters. It is also linked with the condemnation of Origen's speculations on the pre-existence of souls.

days.title: St John of Damascus sums it up

items.text: Book 3 of St John's Exposition of the Orthodox Faith gathers the teaching of the councils on Christ.

items.father: St John of Damascus, Exposition of the Orthodox Faith, Book 3
